CLIPORA / GUIDE

Back up your clipboard history before you need it.

Use Clipora’s password-encrypted export for a portable backup. Keep the password separately and verify the file before resetting or uninstalling the app.

Reviewed 29 October 2026 · Clipora editorial

On this page
Create a password-encrypted backupRestore by merging, then verifyA repeatable backup checkMoving from standalone to Microsoft StoreWhat a backup does not include

Create a password-encrypted backup

  1. Open the Clipora library and choose Backup & restore.
  2. Choose export, provide a strong password and select a destination you control.
  3. Wait for the app’s completion feedback. Confirm the exported file exists at that destination.
  4. Store the password separately. Keep an additional copy on a drive or backup service you trust.

The exported library can contain sensitive copied text and images. Encryption does not make a weak or shared password safe.

Restore by merging, then verify

  1. Open Backup & restore on the destination installation.
  2. Select the exported file and enter its password.
  3. Review the restore action and complete the merge.
  4. Check a known text clip, a pinned item and an image. Paste a harmless sample into a blank document.

Library restore merges items and deletion records. Existing data is preserved unless a newer deletion record applies; matching items can therefore be removed. Settings import replaces settings. Read the app’s confirmation before continuing.

A wrong password or unreadable file should leave the existing library intact. Keep the original backup if you encounter an error; do not delete the destination database to retry.

A repeatable backup check

Before relying on a backup process, create a small synthetic fixture: a text clip named “Backup check”, an example link and a non-private image. Pin the text. Export it, restore into a separate test installation or Windows account you control, and confirm all three items and the pin.

This procedure is a verification checklist for your own backup. It does not claim to have restored your personal data.

Moving from standalone to Microsoft Store

The standalone and Store editions use separate application data locations. Clipora does not automatically import the other installation’s history. Export a portable encrypted backup from the old installation and merge it into the new one.

A raw database copy alone is not a portable backup. The database and key must stay together, and Windows DPAPI protection binds the key to your Windows account. Prefer the password-encrypted export when moving computers.

What a backup does not include

File clips store paths and references, not the contents of the referenced files. Back up those files separately. Windows can remove Store app data during a reset or uninstall; create a verified export first.

Optional sync is a separate feature and is not a substitute for versioned backups. Deleted items can propagate between synced devices. Read the storage, encryption and deletion limits.
